$comment: Test files that do not yet pass on Windows. The `windows-unit` CI job runs the ENTIRE unit suite
on windows-latest — nothing is filtered — and scripts/windows-unit-report.mjs judges the result
against this list (issue #434). Before that job, exactly one test file ran on Windows.
The list is enforced in BOTH directions from that single run: a failing file that is not listed
is a new regression and fails the job; a listed file with zero failures has been fixed and also
fails the job, so the entry must be deleted. That keeps this a shrinking backlog rather than a
permanent hole, and keeps the job a real gate rather than a test of the list itself.
It is a deny-list on purpose: a NEW test file runs on Windows unless someone deliberately names
it here. An allow-list would leave every future file uncovered by default, which is how the
`suspectedProductionBug` marks entries whose failure shows a platform separator inside a value
the product PERSISTS or SERVES (an artifact, a spec reference, a generated path) rather than
inside a test expectation. Those are portability questions about the artifact, not test bugs,

`flaky: true` marks an entry that is NOT deterministically failing — it is exempt from both rules, because a file that oscillates would otherwise fail the build whichever list it sits on. It is a last resort: it needs observed evidence in its reason, it is reported on every run so it stays visible, and it belongs in the backlog issue as a bug to fix rather than a state to keep.
